events.region: Coastal Franklin
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Franklin County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon EDT Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding of coastal adjacent lots, parks, and
roads. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from
shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water will be highest around the time of
high tide, with the next high tide around 730 AM EDT Tuesday.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: South Walton; Coastal Bay; Coastal Gulf
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 11 feet
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...South Walton, Coastal Bay and Coastal Gulf Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT /1 PM
CDT/ Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Wednesday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM EDT /7
AM CDT/ Tuesday to 5 AM EDT /4 AM CDT/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...With minor coastal flooding expected, water around
the time of high tide will flood low-lying parks and roads
along the immediate coast. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water will be highest along the coast
around the time of high tide. The next high tide is around 2 am
CDT Tuesday, with another high tide on Wednesday at 3 am CDT.

events.region: Leelanau, MI
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWAPX

The National Weather Service in Gaylord has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Leelanau County in northern Michigan...

* Until 330 AM EDT.

* At 1133 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas. Some roads
may be susceptible to washing out with high rainfall
rates.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Leland, Empire, Sleeping Bear Point, Bingham, Glen Arbor, Suttons
Bay, Cedar, Maple City, Fouch, Lake Leelanau, Burdickville,
Greilickville, Glen Haven, Peshawbestown, Omena and Good Harbor.

following counties, Harnett, Johnston, Sampson, Wayne and Wilson.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
